column3: Closest parallel: believing action is paired with no fear of injustice or curtailment.
Attentive, silent reception supplies a concrete discipline for hearing that can become response.
Non-curtailment is affirmed within a worldly accounting, while limiting its scope and outcome.
Faithful effort is protected from being denied, a partial parallel to the assurance against loss.
The immediate continuation distinguishes surrender seeking right direction from the unjust alternative.
Names imposed hardship as an overloading of capacity, clarifying the pressure excluded in the focus.
Following guidance is coupled with release from fear, though its fear pair is broader than the focus.
Same-surah counterexample: a sought protection instead increases oppressive burden.
Its gradual diminution and mercy frame fear differently from the believer's assured protection.
Contrasts divine judicial fearlessness with the focus's human, believing recipient of assurance.
Hearing reaches those who believe and submit, directly joining reception to reorientation.
Links unalloyed belief, security, and guidance; it broadens the focus's secure faith condition.
A heard call to belief is answered by belief in the Lord, closely paralleling the focus's sequence.
The adjacent fate of the unjust supplies the contrary outcome within the same local account.
Guidance and mercy are given so that belief in the Lord's meeting becomes possible.
Marks the real division between belief and refusal without specifying the hearing-to-belief movement.
Opens the same narrative with hearing; later cards establish the consequential response.
Treats guidance into belief as a granted movement rather than a self-owned achievement.
Fear of warning identifies a receptive audience but does not articulate the focus's security.
Concrete prohibition of reducing others' due grounds the focus's freedom from deficit in public justice.
Repeats the anti-deficit justice principle, now redundant after the fuller 7:85 card.
Belief upon receiving signs persists under threatened injury, qualifying the focus's assurance amid trial.
Near core parallel: guidance directly elicits belief in the Lord without divided allegiance.
Provides a boundary: fear of disobeying the Lord differs from fear of unjust loss or overload.
Hearing the book recognizes guidance toward truth and a straight way, strongly extending the first movement.
Reports internal diversity without a clear contribution to hearing, belief, or the stated assurance.
Publicly professed belief in the shared Lord turns into an appeal for others to hear.
A concise confession of belief in the Lord confirms the response, but adds little beyond earlier parallels.
The excess imagery is channel-level and does not localize a relevant route to the focus.
Secured hearing before safe return gives reception a protective social condition.
Duplicates the same confession already represented at 26:47 with no additional focus-specific element.
Same-surah boundary: illicit listening is distinguished from hearing that leads to believing response.
Exclusion from a hearing domain is only a distant boundary for the focus's receptive hearing.
Peace is assigned to the follower of guidance, extending guidance toward a security consequence.
Its channel resonance concerns a separate whole-surah reading and offers no localized focus link.
Questions later belief after rejection but gives no distinct account of received guidance or protection.
Believing parents face a future burden imposed through a close relation, sharply illustrating overload.
Same-surah disobedience receives the contrary outcome, setting a moral boundary around the focus.
Divine hearing and knowledge support the setting but do not describe the hearer's faithful response.
Sets hearing joined to obedience against verbal hearing joined to defiance, directly clarifying the focus.
The blocked hearer lacks understanding, providing a negative condition for receptive hearing.
Generic guidance and good news for believers is already specified more directly by earlier cards.
Late belief functions as a boundary case, stressing that response has a consequential timing.
Same-surah denial of any refuge apart from God supports the focus's security as Lord-centered.
The burden verb portrays an advancing, covering pressure, a secondary image for the excluded overload.
Prophetic reassurance against fear is contextually distinct from the believer's paired assurance.
Tranquility increases believers' faith, furnishing an inward security parallel without the focus's two injustices.
Divine hearing is attached to provision and does not develop the focus's reception or assurance.
Fear of following guidance is answered by an existing secure provision, directly testing that fear.
The guarded heaven scene supplies background but no clear focus-specific interpretive addition.
A warning voice bears fear for its people, unlike the believer's stated release from fear.
Ritual facilitation and its lexical overlaps do not supply a localized route to the focus.
The good receive no covering oppression or humiliation, a secondary parallel to protection from burden.
Notes scant belief but lacks the focus's transition from guidance heard to trusted response.
Nonbelief's consequences offer only a broad inverse of the focus's believing security.
Guarding a messenger is not clearly linked to the focus's hearing, faith, or twofold assurance.
Explicitly depicts imposed exhausting ascent, a concentrated contrary image for oppressive overloading.
Commands attentive hearing of revelation, but does not itself show the believing response.
Guidance supports reliance and endurance under injury, showing assurance is compatible with hardship.
Hearing as compliance with corrective procedure is a narrow, secondary instance of responsive reception.
Belief's opposite diverts from the decisive matter, but no direct route to the focus is developed.
Same-surah uncertainty between harm and right direction gives only a loose contextual contrast.
Following messengers with reverence and reform leads to no fear, though more generally than the focus.
Resistance after guidance arrives supplies an inverse condition without clarifying the assurance.
Absence of idle speech does not materially develop hearing into belief here.
Uses responsive hearing as a figure for reception producing change, supporting the focus's active hearing.
Limits future belief among a people but does not explain the focus's reception or security.
Direct negative parallel: claiming to hear while not truly hearing exposes empty reception.
Safety from fear broadens the focus's security, while remaining less specific to belief and justice.
Hearing claimed with disobedience supplies a negative counterpart to hearing that becomes belief.
Addresses believers: hear without turning away, directly binding hearing to obedience.
Tests whether invoked objects hear, a distinct question from the focus's human reception of guidance.
Guidance and ease are present, but the ritual setting adds little after stronger guidance cards.
Even caused hearing can meet turning away, preserving the non-automatic character of reception.
Personal vigilance from fear is not an interpretive parallel to the focus's assurance.
Protective recording prevents reduction of a due, a concrete but now redundant justice mechanism.
Guidance is unavailable to persistent defiance, only broadly contrasting the focus's believing response.
The covenantal formula joins hearing to obedience, an explicit positive model for the focus's response.
Reorients fear within belief, but its adversarial fear setting differs from deficit and overload.
No localized hearing, guidance, belief, or assurance route is evident.
Refusal of signs closes the relation in which guidance operates, defining an inverse condition.
A reduced price is a lexical example of deficit but lacks the focus's believing assurance.
Excluding futile speech is too remote from the active hearing and protection in the focus.
Its marital regulation mentions belief without a relevant hearing or assurance connection.
The divine hearing attribute does not explain the focus's human act of hearing.
Covenantal belief in a confirming messenger is related but lacks the focus's reception or security pattern.
Assured divine listening supports messengers under fear, but only indirectly touches the focus.
No clear link beyond an incidental formal overlap.
Fear for vulnerable successors motivates protective justice, contributing a social form of non-exploitation.
Belief in the Lord under coercion shows faithful response amid pressure, though hearing is unstated.
Hearing, sight, and hearts fail without responsive use, strongly contrasting the focus's effective reception.
Guidance, inward healing, and mercy for believers broaden the beneficial result of reception.
Warning of self-incurred confinement and lack of protector is a broad contrary security frame.
The unjust are not guided; this is a distant boundary rather than a direct focus parallel.
Quranic warning and exclusive devotion relate to belief, but do not add to the focus's central sequence.
Believers' eventual reversal under social pressure is a remote consequence of enduring faith.
The regulation's mention of believers does not connect to the focus's interpretive routes.
Voluntary movement toward the Lord while awaiting guidance preserves a directed trust response.
Rejecting acquisitive increase loosely contrasts excess, but it is not the focus's oppressive burden.
General divine clarification and guidance are too unspecific after the direct guidance-response cards.
Belief, righteous action, reward with the Lord, and no fear form a broad but clear assurance parallel.
Wholehearted surrender and good action receive reward with the Lord and freedom from fear.
Explicitly bars loading a person beyond capacity and adds a protection against reciprocal harm.
States the capacity limit directly, supplying the clearest general boundary against oppressive burden.
God's non-loss of any worker's deed reinforces the focus's exclusion of diminishment.
Divine non-injustice, even at the smallest measure, grounds the focus's assurance against shortfall.
Believing righteous action is joined to entry and freedom from even minute injustice.
Reiterates the belief-righteous-action-no-fear assurance in a distinct communal formulation.
Faith and reform are directly coupled to no fear, closely paralleling the focus's believer condition.
Combines the capacity limit with just speech, bringing overload and justice into one instruction.
The capacity limit accompanies the believing community's promised outcome, though hearing is unstated.
Declares no fear for God's allies; the next ayah identifies them through belief and reverence.
God does not let the reward of those who do good be lost, extending the no-deficit assurance.
Faithful reverence and patience are met without loss of the reward for good action.
Believing righteous action receives a good life and the best recompense, a positive security extension.
The record is read without even a thread's injustice, supplying an accounting-side parallel to no deficit.
God does not waste the reward of good action, directly strengthening the focus's protection from loss.
Pairs a capacity limit with a truthful record in which people are not wronged, matching both justice poles.
Those who affirm the Lord and remain upright are directly told not to fear, extending the focus's trust.
Affirming the Lord and steadfastness are followed by no fear, a particularly close faith-security parallel.
Provision is measured and no soul is burdened beyond what it has been given, directly clarifying overload.
Same-surah abundance after steadiness supplies the material-growth counterpoint noted for non-diminishment.
Same-surah testing clarifies that the focus's no-fear assurance does not mean exemption from trial.
